title: Exclude policy-redacted content from final token accounting
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: Client requests that contain content later removed by the policy/redaction pipeline are currently billed based on the original tokenization. When server-side moderation or automated redaction removes segments mid-processing (either pre-finalization or during streaming), the metering ledger still attributes provisional credits for the redacted tokens. This leads to overstated billable token counts and customer complaints when outputs are suppressed for policy reasons.

Root cause hypothesis: The metering pipeline creates provisional token credits at ingest-time based on the initial tokenizer output and only finalizes or adjusts credits at the very end of the request/finalization path. The policy/redaction stage runs asynchronously and marks spans as "redacted", but those markers do not propagate back to the provisioned-credit ledger in a deterministic way. There is no canonical token-provenance link between redaction spans and ledger line-items, so finalization cannot reliably subtract redacted tokens.

Why it matters: Redacted content is often privacy-sensitive or disallowed, and billing for it violates customer expectations and triggers support escalations. Additionally it creates skewed internal usage metrics and can distort model cost analysis for requests that are largely redacted (e.g., abuse filtering).

Repro steps: 1) Create a request containing a known moderation-triggering phrase interleaved with normal text. 2) Send via streaming API (ws or http streaming). 3) Observe provisional billing event created at ingest. 4) Policy stage redacts the phrase mid-stream (server replaces span with [REDACTED] or removes). 5) Finalization currently reports full token tally; ledger still contains provisional credits for the redacted spans. 6) Query /billing/ledger for session and observe mismatched credited vs visible output tokens.

Observed frequency: ~100% in synthetic harness when policy redaction is triggered; sporadic in production depending on rate of moderation hits.

Immediate mitigation: 1) Add a temporary accounting job to scan recent ledgers for policy-tagged sessions and issue retroactive negative adjustments (manual recon processor). 2) Notify affected accounts and tag for support review. These mitigations reduce customer exposure while we implement the root fix.
acceptance_criteria: Final token accounting excludes server-side redacted token spans across both streaming and non-streaming flows
No double-counting: provisional credits for redacted spans are revoked or replaced before final ledger commit
Audit trail: each redaction produces a ledger event linking the redaction marker to the original provisional credit so retroactive reconciliation is traceable
Unit + integration tests that simulate mid-stream redaction and validate ledger deltas pass in CI
Post-deploy e2e synthetic harness shows <0.1% discrepancy for redacted sessions over a 24h rolling window
tasks: Design: define a token-provenance header format to carry token span IDs through policy/redaction (owner: Marcus)
Runtime: add hooks in the admission path to create provisional credits with span IDs instead of opaque counts (owner: Marcus)
Policy service: emit redaction events containing span IDs and a redaction reason code (owner: Mei Wu)
Ledger service: implement "revoke provisional credit" API and idempotent negative adjustments (owner: Ledger team)
Streaming: ensure redaction markers are emitted via stream frames so clients receive consistent transcript (owner: Streaming team)
Backfill job: small batch job to retro-reconcile last 72h of policy-tagged sessions (owner: Sofia)
Tests: create fuzz harness that injects redaction mid-stream and validates end-to-end ledger state (owner: QA)
Docs: update metering docs and support playbook describing redaction billing behavior (owner: Docs)
Rollout: feature flag and staged rollout to 5%->25%->100% tenants (owner: Release)
Postmortem: record timeline, customer impact, and staff effort after deploy (owner: Sofia)
comments: 2026-03-10 Sofia Patel: Filed after multiple support tickets where customers were billed for content that never appeared in the final output due to moderation. Attached sample transcripts and ledger dumps.

2026-03-11 Marcus Chen: Spike results - proof-of-concept shows we can carry span IDs through tokenizer->runtime with ~2% p99 latency increase in the admission path. Recommend implementing idempotent revoke operation in ledger first.
2026-03-11 Mei Wu: Policy team can emit span IDs, will add reason codes (PII/MOD/etc). Need TTL semantics for redaction markers to avoid unbounded state retention.
2026-03-12 Ledger team: Prototype revoke endpoint merged to PR branch; still needs integration tests and rate-limit safeguards to prevent refund storms.

2026-03-12 QA: Added fuzz scenarios that interleave redaction after partial streaming; some intermittency observed when stream reconnects trigger duplicate provisional credits. Marked as blocker to fix resume-idempotency in streaming layer.
2026-03-12 Sofia Patel: Updated tasks to include backfill job for last 72h. Support notified; holding manual refunds until revoke path is validated in staging.
qa_plan: Create end-to-end harness that runs 10k synthetic requests/day with deterministic redaction insertion points. Validate that ledger deltas match visible token counts and that revoke operations are idempotent under duplicate redaction events. Include chaos tests that simulate stream reconnects and policy service retries.
notes: Avoid changing customer-visible usage numbers retroactively beyond 72 hours without legal review. Coordinate with billing ops for any large-scale crediting. Consider exposing a per-request "redacted_token_count" field in the usage API for transparency.
release_notes_instructions: Runtime: mention policy-redaction-aware metering; Ledger: list revoke API; Console: add redaction count column to session usage table; recommend post-deploy monitoring for discrepancy metrics
